title: Fermilab Muon g-2: a_mu = 116592040(54) × 10^−11, a frequency measurement
summary: The 2021 Fermilab result for the positive muon anomaly is 116592040(54) × 10^−11, from two measured angular frequencies.
body: The abstract of Abi and colleagues states the first Fermilab Muon g-2 result for the positive muon magnetic anomaly a_mu = (g_mu − 2)/2. It says the anomaly is determined from precision measurements of two angular frequencies: the difference frequency between spin precession and the cyclotron frequency, encoded in the intensity of high-energy positrons, and the storage-ring field measured by NMR probes calibrated to the equivalent proton spin-precession frequency in a spherical water sample at 34.7 °C. The abstract gives a_mu(FNAL) = 116592040(54) × 10^−11 (0.46 ppm). It says this result is 3.3 standard deviations greater than the standard-model prediction and agrees with the earlier Brookhaven E821 measurement. Combined with previous measurements of both charge signs, it gives a_mu(Exp) = 116592061(41) × 10^−11 (0.35 ppm) and says the tension with theory is 4.2 standard deviations. The 116592040(54) figure is the experiment's measured result. The standard-model prediction is not rederived on this card.

sources.title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.46 ppm
